Date Certain must be delivered on the specified date and may be driver released only when no Delivery Signature Option applies. Evening Delivery is guaranteed from 5–8 p.m. and may be driver released within that window only when no Delivery Signature Option applies. Time Definite Express services use service-specific commit times that can vary by service, destination type, location, weekday, and Saturday availability. MGB-119 requires delivery by the due time or as soon as safely possible thereafter when timely delivery cannot be made, and a second same-day delivery attempt for packages explicitly identified by the source labels FO, PA, PA+, or M&I.

claim_text: Third-party locker delivery is a driver-release service. Only eligible residential packages designated for release without a signature may use it; signature-required, ASR, hazmat, oversize, and commercial packages intended for residential-complex employees are ineligible. If a package does not fit or the locker malfunctions, contact property management for an approved alternate release location, but do not leave the package on, under, near, or on the floor outside the unusable locker. If property management cannot be contacted or no alternate exists, apply Status Code 007 and return the package to the station. Contact the vendor or property management for a wrong-locker delivery. Use only the provided access code and never share it with an unauthorized person.

claim_text: Current OP-117 states that shippers are responsible for preparing packages for safe transportation with ordinary care. Packages should be new or like-new, with no holes, tears, dents, creases, or crushed corners; old shipping labels and barcodes covered; and all flaps, seams, and edges sealed with at least two-inch-wide packing tape. Its pickup FAQ adds sturdy corrugated cardboard, tape along all seams, and that pickup of nonconforming packages is not advisable. It directs recurring shipper concerns to FedEx station staff and customer complaints or questions to Customer Service, but does not state a universal refusal command for every one-off defect.

claim_text: OP-117 defines activity-specific stop structure. Delivery and pickup at the same location and time is one combo stop with a single signature. Accessible apartment units are one stop per unit; inaccessible units served by one office/mailroom indirect delivery are one stop. Third-party lockers are one stop per customer address. Separate commercial service points requiring separate signatures are separate stops. Combined FedEx OnSite/Office/Authorized ShipCenter HAL/RTH, replenishment, and customer drop-off activity is one stop with one signature. Walmart Recipient Pickup at Store and replenishment delivery are two stops.

claim_text: OP-117 defines on-duty time broadly from readiness to work until relieved of all work responsibility, including station/shipper waiting, inspection/service, driving, loading/unloading/readiness, disabled-vehicle attendance, specified testing, other motor-carrier work, and compensated outside work. Driving time is all time behind the controls of an operating CMV, including traffic and adverse-road delays. It states an 11-hour driving limit after 10 consecutive hours off, no driving beyond the 14th consecutive hour after coming on duty, no driving after 70 on-duty hours in eight consecutive days, a 34-hour restart option, and a 30-minute break after eight cumulative driving hours unless a qualifying short-haul exception applies.

supported_scopes: On-duty/driving classification and normal HOS framework

claim_text: Ready Route cannot establish the complete approved procedure from the supplied sources. Do not estimate or omit work time. OP-117 counts station/shipper waiting, inspections, loading, disabled-vehicle attendance, other motor-carrier work, and compensated outside work as on duty; traffic time behind the controls counts as driving. Stop before any applicable driving/window/break limit and contact HOS/compliance if the totals or an exception are uncertain.

supported_scopes: On-duty/driving classification and normal HOS framework

claim_text: OP-117 states that qualifying short-haul drivers are exempt from the 30-minute break rule. For the described non-CDL 150-air-mile exemption it lists: GVWR under 26,001 lbs.; report/return to the same work-reporting location daily; remain within 150 air miles; specified 14/16-hour frequency limits; and time records. The work-reporting location cannot change during a day. It describes 16-hour exception frequency differently for CDL and non-CDL drivers and says adverse conditions must be unexpected, unforeseeable, and unknown at dispatch. The adverse-condition paragraph contains wording that requires compliance interpretation before any extension is approved.

supported_scopes: Short-haul, reporting-location, 16-hour, and adverse-condition branches

claim_text: OP-117 identifies common disputed-delivery causes and states customer expectations: verify the recipient address before release; scan at the customer location when the delivery or attempt actually occurs; scan every attempt; use the appropriate status when delivery is not attempted; correctly record indirect delivery and its location; scan and complete the Shipment Status Door Tag and leave it visibly at the primary entrance rather than on the package; obtain a required signature; and avoid guessing house numbers, prescanning/in-van scanning, street-visible or high-theft placements, and inaccurate proof-of-delivery information.

supported_scopes: Disputed-delivery prevention, scanning integrity, indirect delivery, and door-tag requirements

claim_text: Verify the actual address and scan at the customer location when the delivery or attempt occurs—never guess or prescan in the van. Follow the package's signature/release rule and record the exact placement. For an eligible indirect delivery, select INDIRECT DELIVERY, record the location, obtain the required signature, scan/complete the door tag, and leave it visibly at the recipient's primary entrance—not on the package.

supported_scopes: Disputed-delivery prevention, scanning integrity, indirect delivery, and door-tag requirements

claim_text: OP-117 links disputed deliveries to wrong/common-area releases, guessed addresses, missing required signatures, inaccurate FRONTDOOR/location records, poor PPOD, prescanning, and incomplete indirect-delivery/door-tag documentation. This is prevention guidance; it does not establish a complete post-complaint recovery investigation.

claim_text: OP-117 states that FedEx prohibits firearms and other listed weapons on FedEx premises regardless of a carry permit or license, except on-duty law enforcement with proper ID; posted standards also apply while service-provider personnel operate equipment leased to FedEx. It lists firearms/replicas, starter or flare pistols, stun guns/tasers, self-defense sprays over 0.5 ounce, and knives with blades over three inches or automatic knives among covered items. Personnel and personal items may be screened on entry or exit, and FedEx may refuse facility access when an individual does not submit. Different/additional law questions go to the local FedEx senior manager.

claim_text: Violence concerns and threats in any form must not be dismissed and should be reported immediately. OP-117 identifies violence on FedEx premises or in service CMVs, vehicle burglary resulting in package loss, robbery or armed robbery, stolen vehicles, and missing vehicles as security incidents that should be reported to FedEx immediately through a FedEx management representative, assigned security specialist, or the 24/7 GSOC. For emergencies call 9-1-1. If an Alert Line report is completed online, retain its incident number for later status checks.

claim_text: The current live MyGroundBiz page requires cargo and load-securing-device examinations, confirmation that cargo is properly loaded and secure, and an out-of-vehicle visual check before operation. Immediately before pulling, personnel must visually verify that dock plates are down or detached and that trailer and dock doors are closed. At a customer location, if readiness cannot be verified visually or with the listed alternatives, the operator should seek customer confirmation and notify FedEx. If neither customer nor FedEx can verify readiness, the trailer must be left and not pulled.
